reason: The 1999 North Central Texas flora has no direct species treatment; do not reuse its Philadelphus pubescens measurements

source.title: Flora of North America, Philadelphus lewisii

source_reported_morphology.stems: Erect to ascending, bark often reddish and exfoliating; axillary buds hidden in pouches
source_reported_morphology.leaves: Petiole 1–6 mm, blades broadly lanceolate to ovate or elliptic, 1.5–10 × 1–5 cm, margins entire to variably toothed
source_reported_morphology.inflorescences: Usually cymose racemes or cymose panicles, (1–)7–49 flowers; sometimes flowers solitary
source_reported_morphology.fruits: Obconic to obovoid capsules, 7–11 × 5–7 mm; tailed seeds ca. 3 mm
source_reported_morphology.phenology: Flowers May–July, fruits June–September within the FNA treatment's range
source_reported_morphology.habitat: Cliffs, rocky slopes, stream banks, pine woodland and forest settings within its reported range

taxon_scope: FNA accepts broadly circumscribed P. lewisii; do not transfer features to P. texensis or P. pubescens
decision: 1999 regional treatment absent, alternate primary flora treatment located and summarized
cautions: FNA treatment's flowering dates are not Hays County phenology
